title: US water protection maps undercount wetlands | Science
description: On 9 September 2026, the US Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) and the US Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) proposed narrowing the definition of “waters of the United States,” limiting federal wetland protection to those touching perennial water. This criterion reduces eligible wetlands even further than the 2023 Sackett v. EPA standard did (1, 2). After the Sackett decision, 19 to 91% of nontidal wetlands were at risk of losing protection, depending on interpretation (3). The EPA’s own regulatory analysis could not produce a reliable national estimate and relied on qualitative judgment instead (4), in part because its National Wetlands Inventory (NWI), which was partially built from decades-old aerial photography, was not designed for regulatory use (4). Obtaining more-accurate and up-to-date wetland maps is therefore essential before revisiting the US rules that define protected waters.
